desc: Political philosophy emphasizing individual rights, liberty, equality, and consent of the governed. Rooted in Enlightenment thinkers: Locke, Mill, Rousseau. Supports democracy, free markets (classical) or social welfare (modern). Foundation of Western political systems.
fact: Individual rights · Liberty · Locke, Mill, Rousseau · Democracy · Classical & modern variants

desc: Political and economic theory advocating social ownership of means of production. Developed by Marx, Engels, Bernstein. Variants: democratic socialism, communism, social democracy. Aims to reduce inequality. Influential in labor movements worldwide.
fact: Social ownership · Marx, Engels · Democratic socialism · Communism · Social democracy

desc: Political philosophy emphasizing tradition, order, stability, and established institutions. Reaction to French Revolution. Key thinkers: Burke, de Maistre. Supports gradual change, authority, private property. Variants: fiscal, social, nationalist.
fact: Tradition & order · Burke · Gradual change · Private property · Authority

desc: Far-right authoritarian ideology emphasizing nationalism, dictatorship, suppression of opposition. Developed by Mussolini. Features: cult of leader, militarism, anti-communism, corporatism. Nazi Germany was extreme variant. Rejected democracy and individual rights.
fact: Authoritarian nationalism · Mussolini · Cult of leader · Anti-democracy · Nazi variant

desc: Revolutionary socialist ideology aiming for classless society. Based on Marx and Engels' Communist Manifesto (1848). Lenin adapted for Russia (1917). Features: abolition of private property, planned economy, vanguard party. USSR, China, Cuba as examples.
fact: Marx & Engels · Classless society · Lenin · USSR, China, Cuba · Abolition of private property

desc: System of government where power rests with citizens through voting. Originated in Ancient Athens. Features: free elections, rule of law, protection of rights, separation of powers. Variants: direct, representative, parliamentary, presidential.
fact: Athens 5th c. BCE · Rule of law · Free elections · Separation of powers · Representative & direct

desc: Ideology emphasizing loyalty to one's nation. Emerged with French Revolution. Key theorists: Herder, Mazzini, Renan. Self-determination principle. Can be civic (based on citizenship) or ethnic (based on ancestry).
fact: Nation loyalty · French Revolution · Herder, Mazzini · Self-determination · Civic vs ethnic

desc: Political philosophy opposing all forms of coercive hierarchy and the state. Key thinkers: Proudhon, Bakunin, Kropotkin. Advocates voluntary cooperation, mutual aid, decentralization.
fact: Anti-state · Proudhon, Bakunin, Kropotkin · Mutual aid · Decentralization · Voluntary cooperation

desc: Advocacy for women's rights and gender equality. Three waves: suffrage (19th/early 20th), reproductive rights/equality (1960s), intersectionality (1990s+). Key figures: Wollstonecraft, Stanton, de Beauvoir, Friedan.
fact: Gender equality · Suffrage movement · Three waves · Wollstonecraft, de Beauvoir · Intersectionality

desc: Movement protecting natural environment from human impact. Roots in conservation (Muir) and preservation (Thoreau). Modern wave sparked by Rachel Carson (Silent Spring, 1962). Climate activism, biodiversity protection.
fact: Conservation & preservation · Silent Spring (1962) · Climate activism · Sustainability · Biodiversity

desc: Principle of separation of religion from state. Rooted in Enlightenment. Key thinkers: Locke, Voltaire, Jefferson. French laïcité, US separation of church and state. Aims to ensure religious freedom and state neutrality.
fact: Separation of church & state · Locke, Voltaire, Jefferson · Laïcité · Religious freedom · State neutrality

desc: Political theory recognizing diversity of groups and interests in society. Multiple centers of power. Unlike totalism which concentrates power. Democratic pluralism encourages competing interests, civil society, and consensus-building.
fact: Diversity of groups · Multiple power centers · Civil society · Consensus-building · Anti-totalism
